newsitem.title: INDIA: Skodaexport's guarantee payment to Indian bank stopped.
newsitem.headline: Skodaexport's guarantee payment to Indian bank stopped.

text.p: BOMBAY, April 14 (Platt's) - A Czech court has issued an injunction to prevent the Czech bank CSOB from paying State Bank of India rupees 1.85-billion ($52.85 million), which is being claimed by Indian Oil Corp as guarantee against Skodaexport's alleged non-performance on the Kandla- Bhatinda product pipeline project, an Indian newspaper reported Monday.

Business Standard added that IOC had moved the court against the injunction. The bank agreement between SBI and CSOB was part of a contract won by Skodaexport over Snamprogretti of Italy following the floating of a global tender in March 1991.

The contract stipulated that the entire job should be completed within 18 months, but the Czech firm had not installed the supervisory control and data acquisition system for the pipeline even after a lapse of 36 months, IOC sources said.
